note: Practical sequence for the trust. Deadlines are from the cited sources. Confirm with a qualified professional.

steps.action: The transfer is treated as occurring on the date of death. Obtain a date-of-death fair market value appraisal, which sets the income-tax basis.
File Form 706 if the gross estate exceeds $15,000,000 (2026). Extension: Form 4768 (6 months). Payment is also due within 9 months. Filing on time is required to elect portability.

Decide whether a beneficiary will occupy Property A as principal residence. Only that arrangement can keep the base value plus the add-on. Rentals, vacation homes and LLC-held property do not qualify.
The occupying beneficiary files the homeowners' exemption claim (BOE-266) with the county assessor. A claim filed by February 15 gets the full exemption for that year.

steps.when: Within 3 years of transfer, or before any third-party transfer

steps.action: Keep the home as the beneficiary's principal residence. If it stops being the principal residence, it is reassessed at the next lien date (value = market value at inheritance, adjusted yearly by the inflation factor).
Check the assessment against the BOE factor (2% cap; 2026-27 factor 1.02) and the value-limit add-on ($1,044,586 through Feb 15, 2027; adjusted every two years).
Insurance: confirm owner-occupied dwelling coverage. FAIR Plan dwelling is an option if the broker's search finds no private market (1-4 unit owner-occupied and rental dwellings are eligible).
Transfer utility accounts. Check the solar interconnection date and the tariff (NEM 2.0 terms run 20 years from interconnection).

Income tax on the gain: federal long-term rates, NIIT (3.8%) above the threshold, and California tax at ordinary rates (no separate capital-gains rate). Basis = date-of-death value (plus improvements).
Check rent-control status and Rent Board requirements before each lease increase (allowable increase 1.6% from 3/1/2026 to 2/28/2027 for rent-controlled units).
